dedupe_keys.name: cascadia rising 2022 exercise washington state after action report and improvement plan

description: Cascadia Rising 2022 was Washington State's exercise series on responding to a no-notice Cascadia Subduction Zone earthquake, with play starting 96 hours after the rupture, and this is its final after-action report and improvement plan. The Washington State Emergency Management Division published it on 18 July 2023, after an exercise on 13 to 16 June 2022 that drew more than 600 participants from tribes, cities, counties, state and federal agencies, the private sector, healthcare, schools and non-profits, supported by FEMA's National Exercise Division. It focuses on critical transportation and mass care services, with operational communication, operational coordination, and logistics and supply chain management, and records observations, considerations and improvement action items to stabilise critical infrastructure and sustain life. Coverage is Washington State. Format and access: an 87-page PDF intended for public release. Licence: public release; free. Caveats: it reports a discussion-based exercise, not a real event, and the first pages read here summarise, not quantify gaps. It supports emergency response and resilience planning for a regional earthquake that would cut roads, fuel and supply chains. A related catalogue record is the Oregon lifelines fragility function database for Cascadia.
